s1@00:30.text: Hi Asha, can you hear me okay? The connection seems a bit choppy.

s1@00:53.text: Before we start, are you happy for me to record this? You can stop at any point.

s1@01:16.text: So to begin, tell me a little bit about yourself and who's at home with you.

s1@01:45.text: And how often would you say you do a proper big shop?

s1@02:10.text: How do you decide what actually goes in the basket each week?

s1@02:36.text: Do you write it down as a list at all?

s1@03:00.text: Is that note something you'd ever print out, or is it always the phone?

s1@03:26.text: Do you set yourselves a budget for the week?

s1@03:51.text: How do you keep track of what you're actually spending?

s1@04:16.text: What happens when the week's plans change halfway through?

s1@04:40.text: Right, that makes sense, thank you.

s1@04:46.text: Can you walk me through the last time you ordered in the app?

s1@05:33.text: How do you feel about substitutions?

s1@05:58.text: How do you choose which delivery slot to book?

s1@06:22.text: Have you ever collected it yourself instead?

s1@06:46.text: If you could change one thing about the app, what would it be?

s1@07:11.text: Is there anything else you'd like to add before we finish?

s1@07:31.text: Brilliant, thank you so much for your time today Asha.

s2@00:30.text: Hello Ben, thanks for joining, let me just share my screen.

s2@00:38.text: I'm going to record the session if that's okay with you, and you can stop it whenever you like.

s2@01:01.text: Could you start by telling me about yourself and your household?

s2@01:26.text: Since you mentioned your evenings are busy, how do you pick a delivery slot?

s2@01:53.text: Has a delivery ever gone wrong for you?

s2@02:17.text: What did the shop do to put that right?

s2@02:42.text: Going back a step, how do you decide what to buy each week?

s2@03:08.text: Which app do you keep your recipes in?

s2@03:33.text: Does anything go from the recipe app straight into your basket?

s2@03:58.text: Do you ever share recipes with your flatmate through it?

s2@04:22.text: So once you've got the list, walk me through placing the order.

s2@04:48.text: What do you think about substitutions?

s2@05:11.text: Have rising prices changed the way you shop at all?

s2@05:42.text: If you could change one thing about the app, what would that be?

s2@06:08.text: Great, thanks Ben, that's all my questions for today.

s3@00:30.text: Hi Carla, sorry, give me one moment while I get the recording going.

s3@00:39.text: Just to confirm, you're happy for this to be recorded, and you can ask me to stop at any time?

s3@01:02.text: Tell me a bit about yourself and who you live with.

s3@06:10.text: Lovely, thank you Carla, that's us done for today.

quotes.text: I live in a terraced house in Leeds with my partner and our two kids, who are seven and ten, so the fridge empties quickly.
Once a week, usually Sunday evening, and then there's always a top-up shop on Wednesday for milk and bread.
I look at what we've got in the cupboards first, then I plan maybe four dinners and fill in the gaps around those.
Always, there's a shared note on my phone that my partner adds to whenever we run out of something.
Always the phone, paper lists just get lost in my coat pocket and then I'm stood in the kitchen guessing.
We try to keep it under a hundred and twenty pounds, but it creeps up every month without us really noticing.
Honestly I just watch the running total in the basket and start taking things out when it goes over a hundred.
Then the vegetables go off, that's the honest answer, and I feel guilty throwing half a bag of spinach away.
I opened the favourites tab, ticked most of last week's things, then searched for the odd extra like birthday candles.
The candles, actually, I searched three different ways and it kept showing me candle-shaped cake toppers instead.
They make me nervous, last time they swapped oat milk for a chocolate oat drink and my son was delighted but I wasn't.
I book the cheapest one on Sunday night, even if it means unpacking shopping at nine o'clock when I'm exhausted.
Once, when the slots were all gone before Christmas, and the car park pickup was quicker than I expected it to be.
Let me lock substitutions per item, so the milk is never swapped but the bread can be anything at all.
It's just me and my flatmate in Bristol, we split some things but mostly shop separately for our own meals.
I pick whatever's free after eight, because I'm never home before then and I hate the idea of a missed delivery.
The driver once left everything with a neighbour I'd never met, and the frozen stuff had defrosted by the time I found it.
They refunded the frozen items after I sent photos, but it took two separate chats with the support bot to get there.
Mostly I follow recipes I've saved, I'll pick three for the week and buy exactly what those need and nothing else.
A free recipe app with a meal planner in it, I've been using it for about two years now and it's full.
No, I type every ingredient in by hand, which is the most tedious part of the whole weekly routine for me.
Sometimes I send her a link when I've cooked something good, but she never actually makes any of them.
I search item by item from the recipe list, which takes ages because the search doesn't understand quantities at all.
I turn them off completely, I'd rather have nothing than the wrong thing turn up when I'm cooking to a recipe.
Yes, I've stopped buying branded pasta and sauces, and I buy meat on the reduced shelf whenever I can find it.
Let me paste a whole recipe in and have the app build the basket for me, with the right quantities already worked out.
I live with my mum, who doesn't use the internet at all, so I do all of the shopping for both of us now.
Mum tells me what she fancies on Saturday, and I add the basics we always need on top of whatever she's asked for.
Eighty pounds is the limit, because it comes out of mum's pension and she checks the receipt very carefully every week.
Every single week, I sort by price per kilo and I'll switch brands without a second thought if it saves us money.
On the fridge, on paper, because mum needs to be able to add things to it herself while I'm out at work.
I'll be honest, I spent most of that order hunting through the offers page, the actual ordering bit was the quick part.
Mum's particular brand of decaf tea, it's listed under a different name in the app and it took me ages to find it.
I rejected it at the door, the driver was lovely about it and the refund was on my card the very next morning.
Massively, the same basket is about fifteen pounds more than it was last spring, and mum notices every penny of it.
Saturday morning, so mum can be up and dressed when the driver comes and help put things away in the right places.
Once it arrived two hours late, which meant mum had to sit waiting by the window all morning, and she was quite upset.
Only that the app should have a simple mode for older people, mum would love to order her own things one day.
